title: Implementer presets allow moving and removing files (with S440)

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Observed 2026-11-11 (slicer s453, ork-20261111-213809-376f): the implementer under `ork projects set slicer --preset python` was denied `git -C <worktree> ls-files -s tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v11.json` and `git mv tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v11.json tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v12.json` while doing the slice's own fixture rename; the run went on. Wanted: decide whether the presets allow `git ls-files` (read-only) and `git mv` (index-only, no commit), or say in the brief that a rename is a plain move the landing picks up.

Evidence (2026-11-18):

- Both presets share one head and tail (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-69`): git `status`, `diff` and `log`, plain and `-C *`, and no `ls-files`, `mv` or `rm`. The built-in default is the go preset (`internal/engine/perm.go:75-78`, adj 75 and adj 94).
- A plain move needs `mv` or `rm`, and neither is in either list, so the implementer today can only Write the new file and leave the old one. ork's commit stages everything (`git add -A`, `internal/engine/states.go:1284`), so a rename done by the implementer by any means is picked up at the commit.
- A preset is written into the registry as a plain list when it is set (`internal/daemon/settings.go:114-120`; `docs/state.md:161`). Changing `ImplementerPreset` changes the built-in default and later `--preset` calls, not a project that already stores a list (slicer does).
- S440 (filed from tool feedback, adj 466 decided `file`) asks for `rm` or `git rm` for the same reason: a file the slice moves out of. S440 and this slice change the same lines (`internal/engine/perm.go:45-69`).
- adj 457 (`launch.allowlist-rg`) dropped `rg` from the presets because `rg --pre` runs a program; the same review applies to any new entry.

Open owner question: which move and index-read forms the presets allow, per the owner's answer to `launch.allowlist-move`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Owner decision adj 478 (launch.allowlist-move = all, 2026-11-18): both presets and the built-in default gain git ls-files, git mv, git rm, and non-recursive rm. Owner decision launch.rm-guard-scope also requires cloud deny rules.

- `TestImplementerPresetsAllowGitLsFilesAndMv` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: both presets contain Bash(git ls-files*), Bash(git -C * ls-files*), Bash(git mv*) and Bash(git -C * mv*). Red: missing entries in ImplementerPreset.
- `TestImplementerPresetsAllowFileRemoval` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: both presets contain Bash(git rm *), Bash(git -C * rm *) and Bash(rm *). Red: missing entries.
- `TestDefaultImplementerAllowlistIsExactlyTheDecidedOne` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go`: exact new default list. Red against old base.
- `TestApprovalAllowsRemovingAFileInTheWorktree` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: git rm cmd/ork/start_unix.go and rm tests/x.py.tail are allowed by the actual presets. Red: missing entries.
- `TestApprovalDeniesRemovingOutsideTheWorktree` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: rm ../other/file, rm /home/x/file and git -C /elsewhere rm f are denied with outside worktree. Existing path behavior is green before changes; mutation-check it.
- `TestApprovalDeniesRecursiveRemove` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: rm -r, -R, -rf, -fr and --recursive never allow through Bash(rm *). Red with explicit new rm entry before hook guard.
- `TestApprovalPathsOnlyKeepsCloudBehaviour` in `internal/agent/claude/pretool_test.go`: with PathsOnly the policy has no Read cap, turns an ask into a deny and grants no read-only own-file Bash; the local policy is unchanged (owner answer launch.cloud-hook-scope, 2026-11-19). Red: paths-only rows keep the local result.
- `TestImplementerPromptSaysHowToRename` in `internal/roles/roles_test.go`: tracked rename uses git mv; files moved out of or created by mistake use git rm or rm rather than stubs. Red: missing prompt guidance.
- `TestArgsCloudRemovalDenyRules` in `internal/agent/claude/args_test.go`: cloud write argv carries --disallowedTools recursive-removal deny rules when plain rm is allowed. Red: flag absent. CLI rule behavior remains unprobed.
- `TestArgsCloudWriteRoleUsesApprovalHook` in `internal/agent/claude/args_test.go`: fresh/resumed cloud writes pass the bound hook in --settings. Red: --settings absent.
- `TestCloudRunnerRemovalApproval` in `internal/daemon/runner_test.go`: the real dispatcher binds cloud writes to the existing approval policy; ordinary removals allow and outside removals, including an absolute symlink escape, deny. Red: cloud argv has no hook settings.
- `TestCloudRunnerHookIsPathsOnly` in `internal/daemon/runner_test.go`: through prepareApproval a cloud implementer reads a 600-line file and an uncovered call is denied by the policy, while claude-local keeps the Read cap. Red: cloud Read capped at 150 lines.
- `TestCloudRunnerApprovalSessionClosesOnError` in `internal/daemon/runner_test.go`: the cloud hook session is inactive after a failed round. Red: no cloud hook session.
- `TestCloudRunnerStopsWhenApprovalSetupFails` in `internal/daemon/runner_test.go`: failed cloud hook setup prevents launch. Red: the round runs without preparing approval. Owner chose option 2 on 2026-11-18: extend the existing approval hook to cloud Claude, retaining recursive deny rules (launch.cloud-remove-paths); option 2 on 2026-11-19: paths only (launch.cloud-hook-scope).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the failing tests and see each red for the stated reason.
2. `ImplementerPreset`: add the adj 478 entries to the shared base, so both presets and the built-in default get them. Keep the order stable; the check command's entry stays last. A part role keeps them (they are not slicer writes, `internal/engine/perm.go:81-100`).
3. Approval hook: refuse a recursive flag (`-r`, `-R`, `-rf`, `-fr`, `--recursive`) for the plain rm entry, so a match on `Bash(rm *)` alone never allows a tree removal. Vet git mv's options the way adj 457 did for rg.
4. Implementer prompt: one line that a tracked file is renamed with `git mv` and ork's commit picks up the move; one line that a file the slice moves code out of, or created by mistake, is removed with `git rm` or `rm`, not left as a stub.
5. A project that stores a list keeps it: the docs say to run `ork projects set NAME --preset go|python` again, or `--allow implementer=PATTERN` (adj 190, adds), to pick up the new entries. ork does not rewrite stored lists.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md` preset lists (cite adj 478 next to adj 75 and adj 94), `docs/state.md:161`, `docs/guide.md:255`. Changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S345 --text "..."`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-18): Cloud claude implementers never run the approval hook, so how far does the recursive-rm and outside-worktree guard reach? -> cloud deny rules: also pass deny rules (for example `--disallowedTools` for `rm -r*`) in `internal/agent/claude/args.go` for cloud runs. This is a new arg path and the CLI's deny-rule behaviour has not been probed. [launch.rm-guard-scope].
Owner answer 2 (2026-11-18, launch.cloud-remove-paths): extend the existing path-checking approval hook to cloud Claude too, retaining recursive deny rules. This replaces the earlier cloud-without-hook premise. Test the argument and launcher/session wiring before implementing it.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:
- The go and python presets, and the built-in default, allow git ls-files, git mv, git rm and non-recursive rm (adj 478).
- A removal outside the worktree is denied; a recursive rm is not allowed by the new entry.
- Cloud Claude argv also carries recursive-rm deny rules (owner decision launch.rm-guard-scope); runtime CLI matching remains unprobed.
- The S350 case (an untracked stray file) and the S431 case (a tracked file the slice moved out of) both have an allowed form.
- The implementer prompt says how to rename and how to remove a file.
- The docs list the new entries, cite adj 478, and say how a project with a stored list picks them up.

Commands:
- `go test ./internal/engine ./internal/agent/claude ./internal/roles -run 'TestImplementerPreset|TestDefaultImplementerAllowlist|TestApprovalAllowsRemoving|TestApprovalDeniesRemoving|TestApprovalDeniesRecursive|TestImplementerPromptSaysHowToRename|TestArgsCloudRemoval' -v`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` exits 0.
- `adj lint` exits 0.
- Cloud Claude write roles use the existing path-checking approval hook as well as recursive deny rules (owner answer 2, 2026-11-18, launch.cloud-remove-paths).
